issues.title: Possible elementary school closures
issues.status: Board of Education vote set for Nov. 16, 2026
issues.summary: The Board of Education is deciding the future of the district's 19 school buildings, which average 57 years old, as part of a Facilities Master Plan begun in spring 2025. A presentation was held Oct. 21, a public hearing Oct. 28, and the full board is set to vote Nov. 16. Enrollment fell from 11,162 in 2018-19 to 9,699 in 2024-25 and is projected at 8,703 by 2034-35. Mount Pleasant Elementary, opened in 1925, is again a candidate for closure; in 2023 the board voted 6-2 to put off that decision for two years. The newest building, Brian S. McCarthy Middle School, opened in August 2024 at a cost of about $93 million.

issues.title: Facilities plan options: keep, close or build
issues.status: Options narrowed; updated plan shown to the board Oct. 21, 2026
issues.summary: Consultant Harriman offered five elementary options. Option A keeps all 12 elementary schools open (about $176 million to $257 million in total). Option B closes Mount Pleasant and New Searles (about $175 million to $218 million). Options C, D and E close two to five older schools and build one or two new ones (about $211 million to $324 million). Every option includes about $62 million for middle and high school repairs. Each school closed saves about $1.6 million to $1.8 million a year in operating costs. Any closure means redistricting and bus route changes. Elementary schools are about 78% full, middle schools about 80% and high schools about 99%.

source.label: Nashua School District, Facilities Master Plan Community Forum #3 (May 20, 2026)

issues.title: FY2027 school budget and 56 job cuts
issues.status: In effect for 2026-27; city budget adopted June 23, 2026
issues.summary: The Superintendent recommended $206.0 million including benefits, up 7.7% from $191.3 million in FY2026 (up 6.0% without benefits), twice the Mayor's 3% guideline. To get there the district cut 56 positions worth about $2.4 million in wages: 21 teachers, 18 paraeducators and behavior specialists, 6 clerical, 5 coaches, 4 administrators and 2 TIA positions.

source.label: Nashua School District, FY2027 Superintendent's Recommendation

issues.title: Elementary special education classrooms reorganized
issues.status: Revised plan for 2026-27; oversight committee requested
issues.summary: The district planned to move elementary special education classrooms for students with intensive and moderate needs among several schools starting in 2026-27. After parent pushback, the Superintendent presented a revised plan on May 11, 2026, and said every school with an intensive needs program would keep it next year. A motion to cancel the reorganization failed, and the board asked its Policy Committee to create a special education oversight committee.

methodology: Built Oct. 31, 2026 from pages opened on nashua.edu and the district's Finalsite documents (Board of Education page and schedule, FY2027 Superintendent's Recommendation, Facilities Master Plan forum deck, 2026-27 calendar, 2024-25 schools and principals list for addresses), the NH Department of Education cost per pupil release, and Nashua Telegraph and Nashua Ink Link reporting. Board officers come from Ink Link's Jan. 5, 2026 report (Jennifer Bishop re-elected chair; Heather Raymond elected clerk, shown as Member because the schema has no clerk role; no vice chair was reported). Term end years follow from the four seats filled in November 2025 (four-year terms, through 2029) and the other five seats elected in 2023 (through 2027). School enrollment is the district count dated May 14, 2025; the 9,526 total is the district K-12 figure from the same date (the 17 school counts shown add to 9,498; Franklin Street has no published count). Grade spans are inferred from district planning slides that discuss moving grade 5 to middle schools and grade 8 to high schools. Principals are listed only for the two high schools, confirmed in an Oct. 22, 2026 Telegraph photo caption; the district's latest principal list is from 2024-25 and several posts have changed, so other principals are left blank. Gaps: no official graduation rate or test results could be read (NH DOE iReport blocks automated access and DOE PDFs failed to load), so results is empty; the FY2025 (2024-25) cost per pupil report exists but could not be opened, so the 2023-24 figure is shown; no closings or delays page was found on the district site; the board's posted schedule ends Oct. 31, so regular November and December meeting dates are not listed. The $206.0 million budget is the Superintendent's request including City-estimated benefits; the exact final school appropriation was not found.
